cards.explanation: The answer is that they had died in Egypt. The whole congregation says, "If only we had died in the land of Egypt…" (Numbers 14:2). They add a second wish, that they had died in this wilderness. The text says the people wept that night (Numbers 14:1), and I think that's a lot of hurt and fear coming out all at once.

The answer is True. The people ask, "Why is the LORD bringing us into this land to fall by the sword?" (Numbers 14:3). I think fear is doing the talking here, friends. When fear grabs the microphone, it doesn't hand it back quick.

The missing word is "leader." The people say, "Let us appoint a leader and return to Egypt." (Numbers 14:4). They say it to one another, so this plan is coming from the people talking among themselves. I think that shows how scared they were, since the plan ends with going back to Egypt.

The missing word is "good." Joshua and Caleb say, "The land we passed through and explored is an exceedingly good land." (Numbers 14:7). Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh were two of the spies, so they're speaking from what they saw. Same trip, very different review.

The answer is the LORD Himself. Joshua and Caleb say, "If the LORD delights in us, He will bring us into this land, a land flowing with milk and honey, and He will give it to us." (Numbers 14:8). The one doing the bringing and the giving is the LORD. That's why they keep pointing at Him and not at the crowd.

The answer is False. Joshua and Caleb never say a word about the army's strength. They say, "Their protection has been removed, and the LORD is with us." (Numbers 14:9). All their courage sits on that last part.

The answer is that they threaten to stone them. Joshua and Caleb tore their clothes and told everyone the land was exceedingly good, that the LORD was with them, and not to rebel or be afraid (Numbers 14:6 through 9). The answer they got was a threat to stone them. I think that one stings. And right then, the glory of the LORD appeared to all the Israelites at the Tent of Meeting (Numbers 14:10).

The missing word is "believe." The LORD asks how long they will refuse to believe in Him, and He points to all the signs He has performed among them (Numbers 14:11). Signs all around, and still the belief won't come. I think that's what makes the question so heavy.

The answer is the Egyptians. Moses says, "The Egyptians will hear of it, for by Your strength You brought this people from among them." (Numbers 14:13). He answers with a plea for the people. He doesn't take the offer to become a greater nation.

The answer is True. Moses says the nations would say, "Because the LORD was unable to bring this people into the land He swore to give them, He has slaughtered them in the wilderness." (Numbers 14:16). Moses is telling the LORD what the nations who have heard of His fame would say. It's a pleading kind of prayer.

The missing word is "pardon." Moses prays, "Pardon, I pray, the iniquity of this people, in keeping with the greatness of Your loving devotion…" (Numbers 14:19). He asks for pardon based on how great the LORD's loving devotion is. He doesn't point to anything the people did to earn it.

The answer is True. The LORD replies, "I have pardoned them as you requested…" (Numbers 14:20). Moses asked, and the LORD answered. It's a good moment to let out a breath, friends, because the next part of the story gets heavy.

The answer is that none of them will see the land. The LORD says, "…not one will ever see the land that I swore to give their fathers." (Numbers 14:23). These are the men who saw His glory and the signs, and still tested Him ten times (Numbers 14:22). It's a heavy verse, and the LORD means it.

The missing name is Caleb. The LORD says, "But because My servant Caleb has a different spirit and has followed Me wholeheartedly…" (Numbers 24 is not this one, it's Numbers 14:24). Caleb son of Jephunneh was one of the spies who said the land was good. The LORD calls him His servant.

The answer is True. The LORD says, "…turn back tomorrow and head for the wilderness along the route to the Red Sea." (Numbers 14:25). He also mentions the Amalekites and Canaanites living in the valleys. Those are the people living in the land.

The answer is exactly what He heard them say. The LORD says He will do to them just what He heard them say (Numbers 14:28). He had heard their complaints against Him (Numbers 14:27). Earlier they'd said they wished they had died in the wilderness (Numbers 14:2). Now the LORD says their bodies will fall in this wilderness (Numbers 14:29).

The answer is False. The LORD says, "Your bodies will fall in this wilderness…" and He says it to everyone numbered in the census who was twenty years of age or older, because they grumbled against Him (Numbers 14:29). So it's far more than the spies. There are two exceptions the LORD names: Caleb and Joshua (Numbers 14:30).

The answer is their children. The LORD says, "But I will bring your children, whom you said would become plunder, into the land you have rejected—and they will enjoy it." (Numbers 14:31). The people had said their children would become plunder (Numbers 14:3). The LORD says those same children will enjoy the land.

The missing word is "year." The LORD says, "…you shall bear your guilt forty years…" and that it is a year for each day (Numbers 14:34). Forty days of spying became forty years. That's a long time to be on the road.

The answer is True. The men who brought out the bad report were struck down by a plague before the LORD (Numbers 14:36 and 37). Two of the spies came through it: Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh (Numbers 14:38). They were the same two who had spoken up for the land, saying it was exceedingly good (Numbers 14:6 and 7).

The answer is that they want to go to the place the LORD promised. They say, "We have indeed sinned…" "but we will go to the place the LORD has promised." (Numbers 14:40). They got up early the next morning to do it. The LORD had told them to turn back and head for the wilderness (Numbers 14:25), so this goes the other way.

The answer is that the LORD is not among them. Moses says, "Do not go up, lest you be struck down by your enemies, because the LORD is not among you." (Numbers 14:42). The reason is the LORD's absence, not how big the enemy is. Moses says it plainly and doesn't dress it up.

The answer is False. The people went up to the ridge "…though neither Moses nor the ark of the covenant of the LORD moved from the camp." (Numbers 14:44). Moses and the ark stayed put. The people went up on their own.

The missing place is Hormah. The Amalekites and Canaanites "…attacked them, and routed them all the way to Hormah." (Numbers 14:45). The Amalekites and Canaanites were the people living in that part of the hill country. It's just what Moses warned them about.
